description: Building software that resists attack across the whole life cycle: secure development processes, threat modelling, the OWASP Top Ten and memory-safety flaws, input validation and output encoding, authentication, sessions and secrets, static and dynamic analysis, and security code review and dependency management. Every vulnerability is first exploited and then fixed in deliberately vulnerable applications running in the browser lab, and every fix is verified with automated tests and scanners.
modelledOn: OWASP Top Ten and the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework
Howard and Lipner, The Security Development Lifecycle
ISC2 Certified Secure Software Lifecycle Professional (CSSLP)
outcomes: Integrate security activities into each phase of a software development life cycle and write security requirements.
Build threat models with data flow diagrams and STRIDE and rate and mitigate the threats found.
Exploit and remediate the OWASP Top Ten and common memory-safety vulnerabilities.
Implement input validation, output encoding, authentication, session management and secrets handling correctly.
Use static analysis, dynamic analysis and fuzzing in a CI pipeline and triage their findings.
Conduct a security code review and manage third-party dependencies and the software supply chain.

units.title: The secure development life cycle
topics: Why software is insecure; vulnerabilities, exploits and the economics of security
Design principles: least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, defence in depth, economy of mechanism
Secure development processes: the SDL, the NIST SSDF and OWASP SAMM
Security requirements, abuse cases and shifting security left
Ghana's Cybersecurity Act and Data Protection Act and what they demand of developers

units.title: Threat modelling
topics: Data flow diagrams, assets and trust boundaries
STRIDE per element; attack trees
Privacy threat modelling with LINDDUN
Rating risk with CVSS and likelihood-impact matrices; choosing mitigations
Threat modelling a mobile money app with USSD, agent and API channels
Keeping threat models current as the design changes

units.title: Common vulnerabilities: the OWASP Top Ten
topics: Broken access control and insecure direct object references
Injection: SQL, NoSQL, OS command and template injection
Cryptographic failures, insecure design and security misconfiguration
Vulnerable components, identification failures and software and data integrity failures, including insecure deserialisation
Security logging and monitoring failures; server-side request forgery
Memory-safety flaws: buffer overflows, integer overflows, use-after-free and format strings; the CWE Top 25

units.title: Input validation and output encoding
topics: Trust boundaries, allow-listing, canonicalisation and safe parsing
Parameterised queries, stored procedures and ORMs done safely
Cross-site scripting: reflected, stored and DOM-based; context-aware output encoding; Content Security Policy
Cross-site request forgery, SameSite cookies and anti-CSRF tokens
File uploads, path traversal and XML external entities
Validating phone numbers, amounts and names in multiple scripts without breaking real users

units.title: Authentication, sessions and secrets
topics: Password storage with bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2; credential stuffing and rate limiting
Multi-factor authentication; the weaknesses of SMS one-time codes and SIM-swap fraud
OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and JSON Web Token pitfalls
Session management: cookie flags, fixation, expiry, revocation and logout
Secrets management: vaults, environment variables, key rotation and secrets leaked into Git history
Applied cryptography for developers: TLS, authenticated encryption, secure randomness and not inventing your own

units.title: Authorisation and secure API design
topics: Access control models: RBAC and ABAC; enforcing authorisation on the server
API security: object-level and function-level authorisation, mass assignment, rate limiting
Secure defaults, safe error handling and logging without leaking personal data
The OWASP API Security Top Ten

units.title: Static and dynamic analysis
topics: Static application security testing: pattern matching, data-flow and taint analysis
Writing custom static analysis rules
Dynamic application security testing with an intercepting proxy and automated scanner
Fuzzing: mutation-based and coverage-guided fuzzers, sanitisers
Triage: false positives, false negatives and prioritising findings
Integrating security tools into continuous integration with sensible gates

units.title: Security code review and dependency management
topics: Manual security code review: checklists, focusing on trust boundaries and authentication flows
Software composition analysis, CVEs and the National Vulnerability Database
Software bills of materials with CycloneDX and SPDX
Supply-chain attacks: typosquatting, dependency confusion and compromised maintainers
Pinning, signing, reproducible builds and the SLSA framework; patch management

units.title: Secure deployment and incident response
topics: Hardening containers and infrastructure as code; scanning images and configuration
Vulnerability disclosure policies and bug bounties
Incident response for application teams: detection, containment and post-incident review
Capstone: threat-model, attack, fix and verify a vulnerable payment application

schedule.title: Why software is insecure and how to build it right
schedule.exercise: Write three abuse cases and matching security requirements for a school fees portal, name the design principle each applies, and list the obligations the Data Protection Act places on the developers.

tasks.title: Review a short login function and mark each violation of least privilege, fail-safe defaults and complete mediation with a corrected version
Write security requirements and abuse cases for a mobile-money feature in a scenario and score them against the coverage rubric
Decide how an app team should handle a request to store national ID numbers, citing data protection duties and design controls, and score the decision

schedule.title: Threat modelling basics
schedule.exercise: Draw a data flow diagram of a clinic appointment app with trust boundaries, apply STRIDE to each element, and list the top five threats found.

tasks.title: Draw a data flow diagram for a school results app and mark the assets and two trust boundaries
Apply STRIDE to every element of a given DFD and record at least one threat per element in a table with a proposed mitigation
Run a privacy threat model with LINDDUN on a health-records app scenario, choose the highest-risk threats, and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Rating risk and modelling a mobile money app
schedule.exercise: Rate six threats to a mobile-money app with CVSS and a likelihood-impact matrix, rank them, and propose one mitigation for each of the top three.

tasks.title: Calculate CVSS base scores for three vulnerability descriptions from given metric values and rank them by severity
Draw a threat model of a mobile-money system with USSD, agent and API channels and mark five threats on the diagram
Update an existing threat model after a design change adding a third-party API, deciding what to re-assess, and score the update

schedule.title: Common web vulnerabilities, part one
schedule.exercise: For three short code snippets, name the vulnerability class, explain how an attacker would trigger it, and write the corrected version.

tasks.title: Identify the SQL injection in a given login query, show the input that bypasses it in the test harness, and fix it with a parameterised query
Fix an insecure direct object reference in a given endpoint so that a user can read only their own records, and test with two accounts
Audit a given small app for weak crypto, default credentials and verbose errors, and produce a prioritised list of fixes with patches

schedule.title: Common vulnerabilities, part two
schedule.exercise: Explain why each of three vulnerable libraries or patterns (outdated dependency, unsafe deserialisation, SSRF) is dangerous, and write a one-line detection and a fix for each.

tasks.title: Run a provided C program in the sandbox with overlong input to see a buffer overflow, then fix it with bounds-checked copying
Replace an insecure pickle deserialisation of user input with a JSON-based design and show the original exploit now fails
Fix a server-side request forgery in a URL preview feature using an allow-list and address checks, and test against internal address inputs

schedule.title: Input handling and injection defences
schedule.exercise: Describe for each of three outputs (HTML body, attribute, JavaScript string) the encoding required, and write a Content Security Policy that blocks inline scripts.

tasks.title: Convert five string-built SQL queries in a given module to parameterised form and confirm the test suite still passes
Fix reflected and stored cross-site scripting in a comment page using context-aware output encoding, and re-run the provided payloads to confirm
Write a canonicalise-then-validate input layer with allow-lists for a file name and URL parameter, and defeat ten encoded bypass attempts

schedule.title: Request forgery, uploads and robust validation
schedule.exercise: Write secure validation rules for Ghanaian phone numbers, cedi amounts and personal names that include non-Latin characters, and justify why strict patterns would wrongly reject real users.

tasks.title: Add an anti-CSRF token and SameSite cookie to a state-changing form and show a forged cross-site request now fails
Secure a file upload endpoint by checking type, size and path, and show that a traversal name like ../../config is rejected
Write and test a validator for names, phone numbers and amounts that accepts 30 real-world valid inputs and rejects 30 malicious ones

schedule.title: Authentication
schedule.exercise: Explain why SMS one-time codes are weak against SIM-swap fraud, compare them with authenticator apps and hardware keys, and recommend a method for a mobile-money agent app.

tasks.title: Replace plain-text password storage in a given module with salted Argon2 or bcrypt hashing and verify login still works for old test users
Add rate limiting and lockout to a login endpoint and show 100 credential-stuffing attempts are throttled while a legitimate user succeeds
Find and fix three JWT pitfalls in a given service (none algorithm, no expiry, weak secret) and verify forged tokens are rejected

schedule.title: Sessions, secrets and cryptography
schedule.exercise: Review a repository history in which an API key was committed, list the steps to contain the leak, and design a rotation plan and a safer secrets arrangement.

tasks.title: Set the secure cookie flags and a session expiry in a given app, regenerate the session ID at login, and test with a fixation attempt
Find a leaked key in the git history of a practice repository, purge it, rotate the credential, and move it to an environment variable
Replace a home-made XOR cipher and Math.random token generator with authenticated encryption and secure randomness, and test tampering is detected

schedule.title: Authorisation and API security
schedule.exercise: Design a role-based access matrix for a clinic API with four roles, list ten endpoints, and identify two cases where object-level checks are needed beyond the role.

tasks.title: Implement role-based checks on the server for admin and user endpoints and show a user token is refused on every admin route
Fix a mass assignment flaw that lets users set their own role, and an object-level authorisation gap, and verify with a test for each
Audit a small API against the OWASP API Top Ten, list each finding with evidence, and fix the three highest-risk ones with regression tests

schedule.title: Static and dynamic analysis
schedule.exercise: Compare what a static analyser and a dynamic scanner can and cannot find, with one example vulnerability for each, and note the cost of false positives.

tasks.title: Run a static analyser over a provided project, count findings by severity, and confirm by reading the code whether the top three are real
Write a custom static rule that flags string-concatenated SQL queries and run it over a codebase, listing the matches it finds
Use an intercepting proxy against a local practice app to find three flaws, record the requests and responses, and write the fix for each

schedule.title: Fuzzing, triage and security in CI
schedule.exercise: Triage a list of 15 scanner findings into true and false positives with a reason for each, and design a CI pipeline with security gates that does not block every build.

tasks.title: Run a simple mutation fuzzer against a given parser function, collect the crashing inputs, and report how many distinct failures it found
Triage a batch of scanner findings by severity and exploitability within limited time, and score the priority order against the rubric
Add dependency scanning and secret detection to a repository's continuous integration workflow, with a gate that fails the build on high severity only

schedule.title: Reviews, supply chain, operations and capstone
schedule.exercise: Carry out a security review of a vulnerable payment application: threat model it, find and fix five flaws, add a software bill of materials, and write a vulnerability disclosure policy.

tasks.title: Review a short authentication module against a security checklist, marking each finding with line number and risk
Generate a software bill of materials for a small project, match each component against known vulnerabilities, and list the ones needing upgrade
Respond as the application team to a reported data exposure incident, choosing detection, containment and review steps, and score against the rubric
Threat-model a vulnerable payment application, attack it in the local lab, fix the flaws found, and verify with tests that each exploit now fails
